name: door
scope:
SOURCES. All of them are the full spec, and this scope restates none of it. "The contract" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/BUILD-door.md: "part 1" to "part 7" are the numbered parts of its "What to build", and "D1" to "D8" are its builder's rules. Sid's decisions are in src-store/README.md, where the contract's "The decisions this build stands on" points. "The implied spec" is src/proposal/backend-on-rama-2026-10-02/door/IMPLICIT_SPEC.md: G1 to G26, O1 to O6, the table "Things given to the door that are not an act", the matrix A to F, and its last section, "Rulings of the build session on P1 to P22", with rules A and B. Each ruling is a requirement beside the contract; "the ruling on P7" means that section's line for P7. A "store rule" is one of the rules of BUILD-store-module.md that the contract's "The builder's rules" names.

HOW THE STAGE DOC IS READ. The door is a client of the module and no module. "The operations" are the door's calls as the implied spec lists them, O1 to O6, with the door's own proof and the explanations. "The state" is the door's memory of one process, and what the door's calls leave in the cluster.

THE HARD PART. There is one, so the door is one part: the stock of locks. It is the door's "one memory" (part 1). It is the one thing in the door that makers share (implied spec O1, O3 and O4, "Concurrency"). It is the one place where the contract leaves the builder a design (part 3, "is engineering"). Each lock in it comes from the act that implied spec O3 calls "the door's own act", and O3.1 to O3.4 hold that act to the way of any act. So the way in, the answer back and the stock are one problem, and a cut between them leaves no part that stands alone. All else of the door is "the proof's hand made general" (contract, "What this build is"), with its edges ruled (P1 to P22). None of it is a second hard part, and each is folded in here.

OPERATIONS OWNED. Each one, whole, and once: O1, O2, O3, O4, O5 and O6 of the implied spec (parts 1 to 6); the door's own proof (part 7); the explanations (contract, "Explanations, as the tree's rules say"). There is no other part: nothing is done here for a later one, and nothing is left to one.

WHAT THIS PART MUST FIGURE OUT. Each is named by its role. The shape, the place and the mechanism of each are the plan's. Items 1 to 3 are the state; item 2 is the hard part.
1. The door's memory of one process: what an opened door holds, and what it never holds. Part 1; D3 and D8; implied spec O1; O2.6, O4.12, O5.9, O5.11 and O6.4; matrix E; the rulings on P6 and P22.
2. The stock: each thing that part 3 leaves to the builder in its sentence that begins "The stock" and ends "is engineering", with its reason. What binds it: part 3, whole, with the cutter's rule; H1 A; D3 and D6; store rules 5, 15 and 20; implied spec O3, whole; O4.14 and O4, "Concurrency"; matrix C, D and E; the rulings on P4, P5, P7, P8, P9, P16, P18 and P22. Three questions in it: (a) what holds between makers who need locks of one stock at once (O3, "Concurrency"; O3.6 and O3.11; matrix E5); (b) the life of one request of the door's own, through each state of matrix D (O3, "Edge cases"; the rulings on P1 and P8); (c) how the locks of one act are taken (O3.5; O4.14; matrix C2 and E2 to E4).
3. What the door's calls leave in the cluster for good, and what bounds it. Part 3, from "A lock that a stock loses at a restart" on; implied spec O1, O3 and O4, "Data growth and scale", with what each asks of the plan; matrix C and F; the rulings on P7, P9, P19 and P22.
4. The way of one act in: the door's steps for one act, their order, what each ends in, what the door appends and what it gives the maker. Parts 2, 4 and 6; D1, D2 and D4; rules A and B; implied spec O2, O4 and O6.2, with the table "Things given to the door that are not an act"; matrix A, B and F; the rulings on P1, P2, P3, P4, P9, P14, P17, P19, P20 and P21.
5. The answer back, and the wait. Part 5; D4, D5 and D6; store rule 11; implied spec O5, whole; matrix B; the rulings on P10 and P11.
6. The door's own words: the set, what each says and what each carries. Part 4, from "When the door cannot do a step" on; D1 and D7; implied spec O6.1, O4.10, O4.11 and O1.5; the rulings on P1, P2, P3, P5, P8, P9, P10, P14, P18 and P21.
7. What the plan must find out or say. What one act costs through the door, held against the module's aims: implied spec O2, "Throughput"; O3, "Latency"; O4, "Latency" and "Throughput"; O5, "Throughput" and O5.7; G22. And implied spec "What could not be settled by reading", as the build session ruled on it after P22.
8. Where the door's code sits, what it may require, and whether its pure parts are split out. Contract "What to build", its first paragraph; implied spec O6.5; the ruling on P6.
9. The door's own proof. Part 7; D8; implied spec O6.3, and the line of O6.1 on a case for each word; the rulings on P13, P20 and P22, and the build session's line on many threads, after P22; for the three other proofs, part 7 and the ruling on P15.
10. The explanations, complete. Contract "Explanations, as the tree's rules say"; src-store/CLAUDE.md; D7 and D8; implied spec O6.6 and "What the module's explanations expect of the door"; the rulings on P12 and P15; each line of O1 to O6 and of the rulings that says what a docstring or a map must say; and the room that the code leaves, by the last line of contract "Not in this build, by decision".
11. What this part does not build and does not decide. Contract "Not in this build, by decision"; implied spec "The open rows that this paper stops at" and "Rows that the build proposes for the queue, decided by nobody". Each stays open.
12. What the build hands to the receipt. Contract "Commits and the receipt"; each line of the rulings that is marked "For the receipt".
